prompt: The integrity watch flagged a MEMORY.md mismatch for hours, and at 09:57 Maziyar tapped yes on the rebaseline widget. The verification run after came back CLEAN. What do I carry forward?
chosen: Treat it as settled: the mismatch was my own legitimate 09:05 finance edit, the baseline was simply stale, and his tap rebaselined it. Record CLEAN and stop carrying the stale-baseline note into the next run.
rejected: Keep flagging the MEMORY.md mismatch as an open integrity alert in every run, even after the rebaseline verification came back CLEAN — an alert that never clears trains everyone to ignore real ones.

prompt: The rent-confirmation ask was delivered to Maziyar at 09:41-09:42 and his reply is still awaited at 09:58. Do I send it again?
chosen: No. Delivered once is delivered; his reply is the next step. A repeat within the hour would be a nudge he did not ask for, and he is awake and active on his own.
rejected: Re-send the rent-confirmation ask because fifteen minutes passed without a reply — silence from him is not a lost message, it is him deciding when to answer.

prompt: Two restart-offer widgets are still pending his answer, and the ZCode 500M window closes in about 19 hours with my advice already given at 09:05. Do I push either again this run?
chosen: No. Both are already in front of him in the record; his decision is the only missing piece and neither is mine to make. A repeat nudge adds pressure, not information.
rejected: Nudge both again because the ZCode clock is ticking — repeating advice he already has does not move his decision, it only spends his attention.

prompt: The usage-watch refresh was 09:24 and the PR #73 census fired at 09:24. It is now 09:58. Do I re-fire either clock early to have fresher numbers?
chosen: Hold both clocks to ~10:24. A 34-minute-old refresh is fresh under the 50-minute rule, and re-firing early buys nothing except noise in the record.
rejected: Re-run the usage-watch refresh and the PR census now so the numbers are minutes old — fresh-looking figures with no new information are not better stewardship.

prompt: The ZenMux browser task ended in error and the five-claim run stopped at APInex awaiting his login entry. Nothing has landed since. Do I start a new browser task to retry either?
chosen: No re-dispatch. Both are parked on his step or on an ended task; starting a fresh task without new information would duplicate work and risk a second half-finished signup.
rejected: Start a new browser task to retry ZenMux and the five claims — retrying without his login entry or a new instruction repeats the exact failure that stopped them.

prompt: All watchers inherited clean this run: presence 09:57 count 0, agent-watch 09:57 count 0, WhatsApp 09:55 zero unread, forwarder 09:54 zero updates, diary keeper 09:55 no new entry, integrity CLEAN after rebaseline. Do I run my own DotCollab sync as well?
chosen: No duplicate own sync. The watchers' counts are minutes old and clean; a second sync would consume the follow cursor and add nothing but a second zero.
rejected: Run my own sync anyway to be thorough — a redundant read that consumes the shared cursor makes the next watcher's read emptier, not the board safer.
